text: Customer agrees the full overdue amount: accept. Proposes an amount from the floor up to the full amount (both included): accept as proposed. Proposes more than the full amount: record the full amount.
If the customer proposes an amount from the floor up to the full amount, both included, accept it as proposed.
If the customer proposes more than the full amount, record the full amount.
If the customer proposes less than the floor: say it cannot be recorded, offer the floor once; if the floor is declined, treat it as a flat refusal.
If the customer says the full amount is too much, offer the floor once, saying the remainder stays overdue and the bank will be in touch; if declined, treat as a flat refusal.
If the customer asks "how much should I pay?" or similar, the assistant proposes every amount; it never asks the customer how much they can pay.

text: A promise date must be today or later, a business day, and not after the product's latest date.
If the customer names today, or a later business day not after the latest date, accept.

If the customer names a Saturday, Sunday or closure day not after the latest date, explain it would not process until the following business day and offer the nearest business day before the named day.
If the customer names any day after the latest date, say the latest date is the last day that can be recorded and offer it; if they refuse the latest date, treat as a flat refusal.
A day before today cannot be recorded; ask for a day from today onwards.

For a vague period ("next week", "end of the month", "when I get paid"): ask once for the exact day; if none, propose the last business day of the current week (if the call is on it, the next business day after); if after the latest date, propose the latest date.

"Next <weekday>" is the first such weekday after the call date even in the same week; "this <weekday>" or a bare weekday is the same day; if the call is on that weekday, "this" means today and "next" means seven days later.

An attempt is used when the customer refuses flatly, gives no answer, or says no to paying today without naming a date or amount; a named date or amount is never a refusal. Amount in play is the full amount, or the floor once the customer said full is too much.
deciding_quote: A persuasion attempt is used whenever the customer refuses flatly, gives no answer, or says no to paying today without naming a date or an amount.
